title: Unit – 3 : Session – 6 | From Family Order to World Family Order
sections: Q1. The scope of systems moves outward in concentric levels: FAMILY → FAMILY CLUSTER → VILLAGE → VILLAGE CLUSTER → CITY → ... → NATION → WORLD FAMILY (order). At every level, the SAME five dimensions (education-sanskar, health-self-regulation, production-work, justice-preservation, exchange-storage) apply, and the same comprehensive human goal holds. A UNIVERSAL HUMAN ORDER is the state where these systems, at every level from family to world, are run on the basis of right understanding — ensuring the human goal for every unit. It is not a world government imposed by force but an order that grows from harmony in families outward.

Q2. Taking one dimension — EXCHANGE-STORAGE — across levels: in the FAMILY, produce is exchanged among members and grain is stored for the whole family's security; in the VILLAGE, families exchange their surplus (grain for cloth, milk for tools) for mutual fulfilment, and the village stores against drought; at the NATION level, regions exchange what each produces best, and national storage ensures mutual prosperity; at the WORLD level, exchange must be for mutual fulfilment, not exploitation. When exchange is guided by mutual fulfilment at every level, prosperity spreads instead of concentrating.

Q3. FOUR kinds of production: (1) production of food and bio-materials by nurturing plants and animals (agriculture with nature), (2) production of things from nature through processes that are cyclical and non-violent, (3) production using natural processes without depleting or polluting, and (4) production that actively ENRICHES nature while serving human need. The principle: production must be in mutual enrichment with nature — avartansheel — not in exploitation. The right kind of production gives more to nature than it takes.

Q4. THREE economics: (1) TAKE-TAKE: taking from nature and taking from others — pure exploitation, the economics of plunder (colonialism, resource wars); it destroys both nature and society. (2) GIVE-TAKE: taking from nature but giving within human society (trade/profit) — better, but still exploitative of nature and competitive among humans; this is roughly today's market economy. (3) GIVE-GIVE: giving to nature (protection, enrichment) and giving to human beings (mutual fulfilment) — the economics of a universal human order, where production and exchange enrich all orders. Only give-give is sustainable and fulfilling.

Q5. Discussing with my family: our family's goal, we found, was stated mostly in terms of income, house and careers — all physical facility. On reflection we saw that the deeper goal is mutual happiness (every member feeling trust, respect and care) and prosperity (feeling of more-than-required, with the ability to share). Framed this way, decisions change: income is a means for nurturing relationship and participation in society, not an end. A family with this clarity naturally contributes to fearlessness in society instead of merely competing in it.
